prompt.context: We have a private equity client that is considering purchasing a small company that makes paintball guns (Splat). Sales last year were $50M, net profit was $20M, and they have been growing at 50% per year. The client has asked us for help in evaluating this investment. You and I are the team members who will do the bulk of the thinking and analysis.
prompt.question: How would you evaluate whether or not this paintball gun company (Splat) is a good investment?

clarifying_info.q: Are there secondary research reports on the paintball gun market?
clarifying_info.a: No secondary research reports exist. You will need to estimate the market yourself.

clarifying_info.q: What percentage of the population plays paintball?
clarifying_info.a: 10% of the population plays paintball in a given year.

clarifying_info.q: What percentage of players actually buy a gun (vs. renting)?
How many guns does the average purchaser buy per year?
What is the average price of a paintball gun?
How fast is the overall market growing?
clarifying_info.a: The market is growing approximately 20% per year and will continue to do so for the next several years.

clarifying_info.q: How do customers evaluate paintball guns?
clarifying_info.a: Customers buy based on reputation for quality. Splat is known as having the best paintball guns on the market. Two other competitors are viewed quite favorably but not as highly ranked as Splat.

clarifying_info.q: What channels does Splat sell through?
clarifying_info.a: Paintball specialty stores, and large chains such as Galyans, Sports Authority, and Wal-Mart. Sales have been steady through the specialty channel but growing about 60% per year in large chains.

clarifying_info.q: Why are large-chain sales growing so fast for Splat?
clarifying_info.a: Over the last few years, the chains have added Splat to a few stores per year. Splat is now in almost all of the stores (rollout is essentially complete). In-store sell-through was growing at 20% across brands, with Splat slightly outperforming at about 25%.

framework: Is the market attractive? Size the market and assess growth.
Can Splat succeed in the market? Assess competitive position, customer perception, and channel dynamics.
What is the valuation / price the client is paying? (Should be mentioned even if not detailed.)

questions.prompt: Estimate the size of the US paintball gun market.
questions.guidance: Walk through a top-down market sizing using population, participation rate, purchase rate, frequency, and price. Show math clearly and arrive at $300M. Then compute Splat's implied market share.

math.setup: Market size = US population × % who play paintball × % who buy a gun × guns per buyer per year × average gun price
math.answer: $300M annual market; Splat holds roughly 17-20% share

questions.prompt: Splat is growing at 50% while the overall market grows at 20%. What explains the gap?
questions.guidance: Candidate should probe customer perception, competitive positioning, and channel dynamics. Key insight: the extra growth comes from rolling out into large chain stores, not purely from share gain or organic market factors. Once the rollout is complete, extraordinary growth will revert toward market growth plus modest share gain (~25%).

questions.prompt: Given your analysis, what is your recommendation on the investment?
questions.guidance: Synthesize market attractiveness (20% growth, large and growing), Splat's competitive position (best-in-class quality perception), and the channel rollout story. Conclude that the store-expansion tailwind is nearly exhausted, so forward growth is likely 20-25% per year. The deal is attractive if the price/multiple is consistent with that normalized growth rate.

brainstorming.prompt: What risks would you highlight for this investment?

categories.name: Market risk
ideas: Paintball could be a fad; participation may plateau or decline
Regulatory or safety concerns could restrict the sport

categories.name: Brand / competitive risk
ideas: Brand perceptions can shift quickly; Splat could lose its quality leadership
Competitors could close the quality gap or undercut on price

categories.name: Safety / legal risk
ideas: A serious injury or death from a Splat gun would create legal liability and brand damage
An industry-wide safety incident (even with a competitor's gun) could reduce overall participation

categories.name: Channel risk
ideas: Large chains could delist Splat in favor of a competitor or private label
Specialty channel remains flat; no additional distribution runway is visible

recommendation: Splat is an attractive investment given strong market growth (~20% per year), best-in-class brand perception, and a demonstrated ability to expand distribution
Going forward, growth is likely to moderate to 20-25% per year as the retail channel rollout is largely complete
The deal makes sense if the acquisition price implies a multiple consistent with 20-25% normalized growth
risks: Paintball participation is subject to fad risk
A safety incident could harm the company or the broader market
next_steps: Confirm acquisition valuation and required return hurdle with the client
Conduct deeper due diligence on supply chain, cost structure, and margins
Assess remaining white-space in distribution and international expansion potential
